newsitem.title: HUNGARY: LOW QUALITY MARS HUNGARY WHEAT EXPORTS - TRADE.
newsitem.headline: LOW QUALITY MARS HUNGARY WHEAT EXPORTS - TRADE.

text.p: Hungary's wheat exports are being plagued by a low-quality crop this year, trade and shipping sources said on Thursday.

"We know that some shipments already in rail carriages have been stopped due to quality problems," Janos Bako, Deputy Director in charge of transport at the national railway company MAV Rt, told Reuters.
MAV officials said last month they expected about half of Hungary's grains exports or some 800,000 tonnes to go by rail.
Last year MAV exported some 300,000 tonnes of grains.

On Wednesday, Hungary's Agriculture Ministry restated its five million tonnes wheat crop forecast for this year, up from last year's 3.9 million tonnes, and said quality problems were of a smaller extent than sources outside the ministry had suggested.
However, the representative of a grains shipping company said their clients had encountered problems in putting together export lots.
"There are problems with the starch-to-sugar ratio," the representative said.
The starch-to-sugar ratio, not included in Hungarian standards, is indicative of the germination stage of the wheat.
Fourteen days of consecutive rainfall have not only delayed harvesting but have also lowered the quality of the crop, the ministry said on Wednesday.
Wheat exports on the Danube are handled by Hungary's national Danube shipping company, MAHART Rt, Ukraine's Ukran Dunahajozas Rt and Romania's Navrom.
Attila Bencsik of MAHART said they had not yet encountered quality problems.
"We have only noticed a drop in transport volumes compared with last year, but that was also due to the delay in harvesting," he said.

The Hungarian representative of a German grains trading company said on conditions of anonymity that several Hungarian grains exporters had cancelled wheat export contracts as they were unable to gather enough good-quality wheat.
"I estimate the cancelled contracts to be somewhere between 100,000 and 200,000 tonnes," he said.
Robert Vajo of Termin grains trading company said August milling wheat deliveries on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) were difficult to honour due to the lack of good quality wheat.
"There are many quality complaints, and these have been hitting almost all traders," Vajo said.
The B1 milling wheat standard of the BCE is somewhat different from the standard for euro wheat.
Both standards set a minimum protein content of 11.5 percent. Hungary's B1 milling wheat has to have a 28 percent gluten content while the euro requirement is 26 percent.
The euro standard also requires a certain starch-to-sugar ratio not included in the Hungarian standard.

An Agriculture Ministry official said about half of this year's wheat crop would be of milling quality but added that he could not contradict reports of difficulties in putting together export shipments of suitable quality.

"The quality of the wheat varies greatly from one wheat plot to the next and it is conceivable that gathering a shipment of consistent quality is difficult," said Deputy State Secretary Jeno Rendagel.
